note: SUPERSEDED by calibration_targets.json (version causal_state_v1/calibration_targets/2). Computed from an earlier version of the public real data, built with a different intervention design (magnitudes, onsets, initial states, pulse durations and silencing persistence differ), with statistics code p4-calibstats-1. Kept for the record; its design-dependent targets do not describe data built with the benchmark's own design.
source: PUBLIC real-system trajectories only (event-free trajectories under nominal input, input-amplitude changes, initial-state changes and structural weight noise; single- and multi-target kicks, current pulses and single-unit silencing on public targets, each validation intervention with its counterfactual twin). No hidden data, no hidden targets, no evaluation output.

classes.full: a full recurrent network (about 200 observed units, 9-20 readout units, one input)
classes.mechanism: a small candidate sub-circuit (3-6 observed units) of such a network, with the same readout and input

check_rule: compare(): a checked statistic is ok when the fraction of synthetic systems inside target_range is >= min_inside_frac, the suite's [min, max] overlaps the real [min, max], and the coverage condition (suite min <= a, suite max >= b) holds when given.

rules.pos: [min / 2, 2 x max] (a factor-2 margin on both sides of the real range)

caveats: The public trajectories are deterministic simulations. The measurable noise floor is the integration-path difference between an intervention trajectory and its twin before the first event (8e-6 to 3e-4 of the rate scale); observation noise is a benchmark parameter, not a property of the real systems.
Current magnitudes are in the simulator's input units; their relation to a unit's threshold is not published, so only their effects are calibrated.
Single-unit time constants are not published; persistence is estimated from the kicked unit's own decay (self_decay_s).
Statistics from few pairs (19 per small system, 40 per large system) are noisy; the per-system values are medians over pairs.
Oscillation: every real system oscillates (7-17 Hz). The autocorrelation decay is then about a quarter period, not a memory time.
Ten systems in two classes are few; the recommended ranges widen the real range by a stated rule rather than fitting it.

acf_censored_frac.definition: fraction of units whose autocorrelation stays above 1/e for half the window (slow drift / persistent activity)

acf_decay_s_median.definition: median over active units and event-free trajectories of the lag (s) at which the autocorrelation first drops below 1/e (window after the onset transient); uncensored units only. For oscillating units this is about a quarter period, not a memory time
acf_decay_s_median.rule: [min / 2, 2 x max] (a factor-2 margin on both sides of the real range)
acf_decay_s_median.rationale: Decorrelation within 12-29 ms (a quarter period of the oscillation where one is present).

acf_decay_s_p10.definition: 10th percentile of the autocorrelation decay lag (s), censored values included

acf_decay_s_p90.definition: 90th percentile of the autocorrelation decay lag (s), censored values included

frac_eff_rel_y_below_0.001_silence.definition: fraction of pairs whose relative readout effect eff_rel_y is below the threshold (near-zero effects)

frac_eff_rel_y_below_0.01.definition: fraction of pairs whose relative readout effect eff_rel_y is below the threshold (near-zero effects)
frac_eff_rel_y_below_0.01.rationale: Near-zero readout effects are common in the large systems (35-45 % of interventions change the readout by < 1 % of its variability) and absent in the small ones. The suite must contain both regimes (a system with none and one with >= 30 % near-zero effects).

frac_eff_rel_y_below_0.01_current.definition: fraction of pairs whose relative readout effect eff_rel_y is below the threshold (near-zero effects)

frac_eff_rel_y_below_0.01_kick.definition: fraction of pairs whose relative readout effect eff_rel_y is below the threshold (near-zero effects)

frac_eff_rel_y_below_0.01_silence.definition: fraction of pairs whose relative readout effect eff_rel_y is below the threshold (near-zero effects)

frac_eff_rel_y_below_0.1.definition: fraction of pairs whose relative readout effect eff_rel_y is below the threshold (near-zero effects)

frac_eff_rel_y_below_0.1_current.definition: fraction of pairs whose relative readout effect eff_rel_y is below the threshold (near-zero effects)

frac_eff_rel_y_below_0.1_kick.definition: fraction of pairs whose relative readout effect eff_rel_y is below the threshold (near-zero effects)

frac_eff_rel_y_below_0.1_silence.definition: fraction of pairs whose relative readout effect eff_rel_y is below the threshold (near-zero effects)

frac_readout_active.definition: fraction of readout units whose temporal sd exceeds 1e-3 s_y
frac_readout_active.rationale: Part of the readout is silent in the small systems; all of it is active in the large ones.

frac_samples_at_floor.definition: fraction of samples of active units at their lower bound (within 1e-6 s_x of the unit's minimum; rectified units at 0)
frac_samples_at_floor.rationale: Rectification: the large systems spend 53-63 % of active-unit samples at the floor, the small ones about 10 %.

frac_samples_near_system_max.definition: fraction of samples of active units at >= 90 % of the largest value of any unit (saturation proxy)

frac_samples_near_unit_max.definition: fraction of samples of active units at >= 90 % of that unit's own maximum

frac_units_active.definition: fraction of observed units whose temporal sd over all records exceeds 1e-3 s_x

input_gain_elasticity_x.definition: slope of log(response RMS during the input) against log(input scale) over event-free trajectories
input_gain_elasticity_x.rule: [min / 2, 2 x max] (a factor-2 margin on both sides of the real range)
input_gain_elasticity_x.rationale: Strongly nonlinear input response: RMS activity grows as the 2.7-5.8th power of the input scale over the public range.

input_gain_elasticity_y.definition: slope of log(response RMS during the input) against log(input scale) over event-free trajectories
input_gain_elasticity_y.rule: [min / 2, 2 x max] (a factor-2 margin on both sides of the real range)

input_response_rms_x_rel_scale_median.definition: RMS of the response during the input divided by the scale (s_x or s_y); median

input_response_rms_y_rel_scale_median.definition: RMS of the response during the input divided by the scale (s_x or s_y); median

input_scale_max.definition: largest input scale in the event-free records

input_scale_min.definition: smallest non-zero input scale in the event-free records

kick_clipped_frac.definition: fraction of single-target first kicks that were clipped at the lower bound

kick_clipped_frac_all.definition: fraction of kick offsets on observed targets (all records) that were clipped at the lower bound
kick_clipped_frac_all.rationale: About a quarter to a half of all public kick offsets are clipped at the floor (negative kicks on units at or near rest).

kick_rel_scale_p5.definition: |kick offset| / s_x for single-target first kicks; percentiles

kick_rel_scale_p50.definition: |kick offset| / s_x for single-target first kicks; percentiles
kick_rel_scale_p50.rule: [min / 2, 2 x max] (a factor-2 margin on both sides of the real range)
kick_rel_scale_p50.rationale: Public kick offsets are 0.1-2 x the system's rate scale.

kick_rel_scale_p95.definition: |kick offset| / s_x for single-target first kicks; percentiles

latency_y_peak_s_current_median.definition: time (s) from the first event's onset to the peak of the readout effect norm within the first-event window; median over pairs

latency_y_peak_s_kick_median.definition: time (s) from the first event's onset to the peak of the readout effect norm within the first-event window; median over pairs

latency_y_peak_s_median.definition: time (s) from the first event's onset to the peak of the readout effect norm within the first-event window; median over pairs
latency_y_peak_s_median.rule: [min / 2, 2 x max] (a factor-2 margin on both sides of the real range)
latency_y_peak_s_median.rationale: Readout effects peak 50-380 ms after the intervention onset (delayed consequences; goal5 section 44).

latency_y_peak_s_silence_median.definition: time (s) from the first event's onset to the peak of the readout effect norm within the first-event window; median over pairs

n_obs.definition: number of observed units (columns of x)
n_obs.rationale: The real systems come in two regimes (3-6 observed units, and about 200). The suite must contain both: at least one system with <= 6 and at least one with >= 100 observed units.

n_targets_public.definition: number of units that development interventions may target

noise_floor_abs.definition: noise floor = max(pre-event difference, float32 resolution x s_x) (units of x)

noise_floor_pre_event_maxabs.definition: largest |x_int - x_twin| before the first event over all pairs (numerical reproducibility of the simulator)

onset_latency_10pct_s.definition: time (s) from the input onset until ||x(t) - x(onset)|| first reaches 10 % of its maximum (nominal trajectories)
onset_latency_10pct_s.rule: [min / 2, 2 x max] (a factor-2 margin on both sides of the real range)
onset_latency_10pct_s.rationale: Responses to the input onset start within 22-54 ms.

params_param_spread_x_abs_rms.definition: spread across parameter draws: nominal trajectories aligned at the input onset; rel_level = RMS(sd over draws) / RMS(mean over draws); rel_dynamics = RMS(sd) / RMS(mean - its time average); abs_rms in units of x / y

params_param_spread_x_rel_dynamics.definition: spread across parameter draws: nominal trajectories aligned at the input onset; rel_level = RMS(sd over draws) / RMS(mean over draws); rel_dynamics = RMS(sd) / RMS(mean - its time average); abs_rms in units of x / y
params_param_spread_x_rel_dynamics.rule: [min / 2, 2 x max] (a factor-2 margin on both sides of the real range)
params_param_spread_x_rel_dynamics.rationale: The spread exceeds the dynamic range of the draw-averaged trajectory (1.3-5.0 x): draws dephase oscillations.

params_param_spread_x_rel_level.definition: spread across parameter draws: nominal trajectories aligned at the input onset; rel_level = RMS(sd over draws) / RMS(mean over draws); rel_dynamics = RMS(sd) / RMS(mean - its time average); abs_rms in units of x / y
params_param_spread_x_rel_level.rule: [min / 2, 2 x max] (a factor-2 margin on both sides of the real range)
params_param_spread_x_rel_level.rationale: Parameter draws change trajectories substantially (spread 0.2-1.2 of the mean level).

params_param_spread_y_abs_rms.definition: spread across parameter draws: nominal trajectories aligned at the input onset; rel_level = RMS(sd over draws) / RMS(mean over draws); rel_dynamics = RMS(sd) / RMS(mean - its time average); abs_rms in units of x / y

params_param_spread_y_rel_dynamics.definition: spread across parameter draws: nominal trajectories aligned at the input onset; rel_level = RMS(sd over draws) / RMS(mean over draws); rel_dynamics = RMS(sd) / RMS(mean - its time average); abs_rms in units of x / y

params_param_spread_y_rel_level.definition: spread across parameter draws: nominal trajectories aligned at the input onset; rel_level = RMS(sd over draws) / RMS(mean over draws); rel_dynamics = RMS(sd) / RMS(mean - its time average); abs_rms in units of x / y

peak_rate_max.definition: percentile across active observed units of each unit's maximum (units of x); _max = the largest

peak_rate_p5.definition: percentile across active observed units of each unit's maximum (units of x); _max = the largest

peak_rate_p50.definition: percentile across active observed units of each unit's maximum (units of x); _max = the largest

peak_rate_p95.definition: percentile across active observed units of each unit's maximum (units of x); _max = the largest

peak_rate_rel_p5.definition: percentile across active observed units of each unit's maximum, divided by s_x

peak_rate_rel_p50.definition: percentile across active observed units of each unit's maximum, divided by s_x
peak_rate_rel_p50.rule: [min / 2, 2 x max] (a factor-2 margin on both sides of the real range)
peak_rate_rel_p50.rationale: Per-unit peaks are 1-4 x the system scale (heterogeneous peak rates).

peak_rate_rel_p95.definition: percentile across active observed units of each unit's maximum, divided by s_x

persistence_ratio_kick.definition: median network effect decay time after kicks divided by the median decay of the kicked unit's own effect (recurrent persistence)
persistence_ratio_kick.rule: [min / 2, 2 x max] (a factor-2 margin on both sides of the real range)
persistence_ratio_kick.rationale: Network effect decay after kicks is 0.9-2.1 x the kicked unit's own decay.

rate_active_p25.definition: percentile of the samples of active observed units that are above the floor (units of x)

rate_active_rel_p5.definition: percentile of the samples of active observed units that are above the floor, divided by s_x

rate_active_rel_p50.definition: percentile of the samples of active observed units that are above the floor, divided by s_x
rate_active_rel_p50.rule: [min / 2, 2 x max] (a factor-2 margin on both sides of the real range)
rate_active_rel_p50.rationale: Median activity of active units is a small fraction of the rate scale (sparse, bursty activity).

rate_active_rel_p75.definition: percentile of the samples of active observed units that are above the floor, divided by s_x

snr_floor_x_median.definition: median over pairs of the effect RMS in x divided by the noise floor

snr_param_x_median.definition: median over pairs of the effect RMS in x divided by the RMS spread of x across parameter draws (nominal trajectories)
snr_param_x_median.rule: [min / 2, 2 x max] (a factor-2 margin on both sides of the real range)
snr_param_x_median.rationale: Intervention effects relative to the spread across parameter draws: 0.16-0.24 (large), 0.5-2.3 (small).

snr_param_y_median.rule: [min / 2, 2 x max] (a factor-2 margin on both sides of the real range)
snr_param_y_median.rationale: The same for the readout: 0.013-0.12 (large), 0.3-0.9 (small); effects are often small compared with parameter variability.

snr_param_y_p10.definition: 10th percentile of the same ratio for the readout

spec_x_f05.definition: Welch spectrum of the active units of x after the onset transient, each unit normalised to unit power, averaged: dominant frequency f_peak (Hz), prominence_log10 (log10 of peak / median density), centroid (Hz), f05 / f50 / f95 (Hz at 5 / 50 / 95 % cumulative power); median over event-free trajectories

spec_x_f50.definition: Welch spectrum of the active units of x after the onset transient, each unit normalised to unit power, averaged: dominant frequency f_peak (Hz), prominence_log10 (log10 of peak / median density), centroid (Hz), f05 / f50 / f95 (Hz at 5 / 50 / 95 % cumulative power); median over event-free trajectories

spec_x_f95.definition: Welch spectrum of the active units of x after the onset transient, each unit normalised to unit power, averaged: dominant frequency f_peak (Hz), prominence_log10 (log10 of peak / median density), centroid (Hz), f05 / f50 / f95 (Hz at 5 / 50 / 95 % cumulative power); median over event-free trajectories

spec_x_f_peak.definition: Welch spectrum of the active units of x after the onset transient, each unit normalised to unit power, averaged: dominant frequency f_peak (Hz), prominence_log10 (log10 of peak / median density), centroid (Hz), f05 / f50 / f95 (Hz at 5 / 50 / 95 % cumulative power); median over event-free trajectories
spec_x_f_peak.rule: [min / 2, 2 x max] (a factor-2 margin on both sides of the real range)
spec_x_f_peak.rationale: All ten real systems oscillate, with dominant frequencies of 7-17 Hz. At least a quarter of the synthetic systems should have their dominant frequency in the target band; families that do not oscillate by construction are exempt.

spec_x_oscillatory_frac.definition: fraction of event-free trajectories whose unit-averaged normalised power spectrum has a peak >= 10 x its median
spec_x_oscillatory_frac.rationale: Every real system is oscillatory; at least a quarter of the synthetic systems should be.

spec_x_prominence_log10.definition: Welch spectrum of the active units of x after the onset transient, each unit normalised to unit power, averaged: dominant frequency f_peak (Hz), prominence_log10 (log10 of peak / median density), centroid (Hz), f05 / f50 / f95 (Hz at 5 / 50 / 95 % cumulative power); median over event-free trajectories
